 Zee5 scores as FIFA kicks Zee’s revenue up 13 per cent
 Digital revenue doubles to Rs 630 crore, but the bill for football and new bets squeezes the Ebitda margin to 3.2 per cent
 Published
 6 hours ago on
 November 1, 2026 
 By
 indiantelevision.com Team 
 Follow us on Google News 
 Follow us on WhatsApp 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 MUMBAI: Football came home to Zee in the July to September quarter. It parked itself on Zee5, ordered a subscription and stayed on for the soaps.
 Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd (ZEEL) grew operating revenue 13 per cent year on year in Q2 FY27. The World Cup did the heavy lifting. The cost of buying the World Cup did the heavy damage. Ebitda came in at Rs 70.8 crore, a thin 3.2 per cent margin. Profit after tax stood at Rs 45.6 crore.
 “The second quarter of this financial year was one of growth,” chief executive officer Punit Goenka told analysts on the earnings call. He asked them to view the sports spend “with a long-term lens”. Translation: don’t judge the striker by one match.
 Digital hits the back of the net 
 Zee5 was the star of the show. Digital revenue more than doubled year on year and jumped 37 per cent over the previous quarter to Rs 630 crore, the highest quarterly haul the vertical has ever booked.
 Even after a fat marketing bill, the digital business delivered Ebitda of Rs 41.6 crore. Deputy chief executive officer and chief financial officer Mukund Galgali said the unit economics remain strong and he expects the momentum to carry into the second half.
 The FIFA numbers were loud. Full tournament reach rose about 41 per cent over the previous World Cup, despite matches landing at odd hours for Indian viewers. Total reach across platforms crossed 400 million, and around 83 per cent of FIFA viewing was live on Zee5. Zee holds the FIFA rights till 2034. It has also picked up Germany’s Bundesliga and Italy’s Serie A for India for five years.
 The streamer also dropped 34 shows and films in the quarter, nine of them Zee5 originals, and gave its app a makeover on mobile and connected TV with AI-led discovery and sharper personalisation.
 Will the football fans stick? 
 That was the question on every analyst’s lips. Subscription revenue rose 30 per cent year on year, helped by higher realisations and more subscribers on digital and price hikes on linear TV.
 Galgali said 35 to 40 per cent of the subscribers who walked in for FIFA have renewed. Most World Cup packs were quarterly, not annual, so the bump will taper. Management admitted subscription growth will not stay at 30 per cent but promised a faster run rate than before from H2 onwards.
 Zee kept mum on exactly how much FIFA brought in, saying only that the numbers were healthy and that most of it showed up as subscription money. Football, the management pointed out, leaves little airtime to sell to advertisers. The bigger linear payoff from the new sports channels will come next year, when distribution deals come up for renegotiation.
 Ads stop bleeding 
 Advertising revenue was flat year on year. That counts as good news at Zee these days. The festive season slid into Q3 this year, yet FIFA and the flagship singing show Sa Re Ga Ma Pa kept ad sales steady. Sequentially, ad revenue grew 20 per cent as tension in the Middle East eased and advertisers crept back.
 Goenka said the slide in ad revenue had stabilised, despite high inflation and a weak monsoon denting consumer mood. Zee’s linear network share hit 20 per cent in week 24, its best in seven years, according to the last available industry ratings before measurement was paused. Monthly reach across genres has crossed 800 million.
 Costs go up, margins go down 
 Operating costs climbed 18 per cent, driven by advertising and publicity spends and the price tag of FIFA. Zee is also pouring money into newer bets such as kids content, live experiences, animation and micro dramas through its Bullet platform, which now has an AI filmmaking tool for creators and studios.
 Strip out the spending on new ventures and the margin would have been in the mid to high single digits, said Galgali. Investors will want to see that in the actual numbers, not the footnotes.
 Studios slow, music hums 
 Zee Studios had a quiet quarter with six releases, one in Hindi and five in other languages. Other sales and services fell 36 per cent year on year against a big syndication deal in the base. The studio did pick up the international distribution rights to Drishyam 3, which released in Q3.
 Zee Music Company racked up over 59 billion video views and has more than 179 million YouTube subscribers. Profits there remain healthy. A separate disclosure, or a value unlock, is another matter. Goenka said Zee is working on segment reporting for several verticals but would not commit to a timeline.
 Cash in the kitty 
 The promoters put in Rs 740 crore as the first tranche of their preferential warrants after shareholders gave the nod. Cash and treasury investments stood at Rs 2,570 crore at the end of September. Galgali said FCCB payments and the dividend payout, not receivables, were what dented cash during the quarter.
 For the rest of FY27, Zee calls itself “cautiously optimistic,” banking on the festive season and its new content slate to lift both revenue and profit.
 The World Cup is over and the crowd has gone home. Zee now has to prove the 40 per cent who stayed back are not just extra time.
